bull.b: Rapid growth in marketed product revenue, led by AMVUTTRA and the TTR franchise, demonstrates strong commercial adoption. This expanding revenue base can improve operating leverage and support sustained investment in Alnylam’s platform and pipeline.

The shift to meaningful profitability and strong cash conversion strengthens internal funding capacity. High free cash flow can support clinical development, commercialization, manufacturing, and strategic investments without relying entirely on external capital.

A growing prescriber base and strong share of new patient starts indicate increasing physician adoption and franchise penetration. High adherence and broader geographic distribution can support recurring treatment demand beyond the initial launch phase.

bear.b: The guidance reduction shows that early launch demand was partly supported by pent-up switching activity and may not persist at the same rate. A slower underlying growth trajectory could limit revenue visibility and increase execution pressure.

Higher royalty rates and ongoing net price reductions can constrain product profitability as sales expand. If these pressures persist, Alnylam may need continued revenue growth to offset weaker unit economics and protect operating margins.

Although the balance sheet has improved, meaningful debt and sharply rising development and launch costs reduce financial flexibility. The company must sustain its recent earnings improvement while funding multiple late-stage programs and commercial expansion.
